quizzes.evaluation: Answer all questions and add up your scores for each of the five sections, then total them. Each section is scored out of 30, and the maximum total is 150. 120–150 — your relationships are getting deliberate attention and it shows in more than one dimension. 80–119 — a working level. The skills are present; what varies is whether they hold up under strain, which is when they matter. Below 80 — relationship maintenance is not yet something you do on purpose. Start with the section that scored lowest rather than with the whole chapter of tips. Then read the five section scores separately, ignoring the total. Any section at 25 or above is a strength other people can already rely on. Any section below 16 is where this month's attention belongs, whatever the total said. Trustworthiness and Respect tend to move together, and a gap between Empathy and Communication usually means you understand more than you say out loud — which the other person cannot read from the outside. Focus on areas with the lowest scores and where results are not meeting expectations. Taking a quiz regularly helps track progress over time.

quizzes.quiz_title: Self-Assessment on Motivation and Goal Setting
quizzes.instructions: Read each statement and rate yourself on a scale of 1 to 3 where 1 = rarely, 2 = sometimes, 3 = often.

quizzes.evaluation: Add up your scores for each of the five sections, then total them. Each section is scored out of 30, and the maximum total is 150. 120–150 — motivation is something you manage rather than something that happens to you. 80–119 — a working level. The methods are there; what varies is whether they hold up in the third week, which is where most goals are lost. Below 80 — start with the three tools at the end of the previous chapter rather than with the tips. Then read the five section scores separately, ignoring the total. Any section at 25 or above is a strength to build on. Any section below 16 is where the next month belongs, whatever the total said. Watch the gap between Goal Clarity and Persistence in particular: a high Clarity score with a low Persistence score is the most common profile there is, and it means the problem is not that you do not know what you want. Focus on areas where your self-assessment scores fall short of expectations, especially those with the lowest scores. Carefully analyze these weaknesses and develop strategies to improve them. Taking this assessment regularly will help you track your progress over time.
